title: CNC Maintenance Technician I - Gallatin
description:
CNC Technician

Beretta U.S.A. Corp.

Reports To: Manufacturing Supervisor

Position Summary

At Beretta U.S.A., our CNC Technicians play a key role in producing the highest-quality firearms in the industry. This is a hands-on, high-impact position for a skilled CNC professional who enjoys more than simply operating equipment. In this role, you will directly support production, troubleshoot machining issues, assist with quality control, guide operators, support basic maintenance needs, and help drive continuous improvement on the manufacturing floor.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who takes pride in precision work, enjoys solving problems in real time, and wants to be a trusted technical resource in a fast-paced 24-hour manufacturing environment. The right candidate will be comfortable moving between CNC machines, tooling systems, inspection requirements, shop-floor support, and computer-based reporting.

Key Responsibilities

CNC Operation, Setup & Production Support

- Operate CNC mills, lathes, grinders, and machining centers as required to support production needs.
- Position raw material or substrates in vises, fixtures, lathes, milling machines, or other CNC equipment.
- Set controls, monitor the machining process, and ensure machines run in a steady, continuous manner.
- Operate multiple CNC machine centers and support multiple workstations when needed.
- Perform duties of operators as required to maintain production flow and meet output requirements.
- Keep count of parts produced daily and help hold shift operators accountable for quality and productivity expectations.

Quality, Inspection & Process Control

- Produce parts that meet Beretta U.S.A. quality specifications while following standard operating procedures and production requirements.
- Use calibrated instruments, tolerance gauges, CMM reports, blueprints, process sheets, and other graphic instructions to verify product quality.
- Make tool changes and tool offset adjustments based on gauging results, CMM readouts, and observed machining conditions.
- Inspect parts for abnormalities and identify broken, dull, or worn tooling before quality issues escalate.
- Ensure highly accurate parts are produced and communicate errors in production, quality, or performance to the immediate supervisor.

Troubleshooting, Tooling & Technical Support

- Identify, analyze, and resolve problems related to CNC machining operations.
- Detect problems by listening for abnormal sounds, recognizing excessive vibration, monitoring lubrication and cooling, and observing machine performance.
- Properly assemble, preset, monitor, and manage tooling to be loaded into CNC machines.
- Read and interpret engineering blueprints, basic CNC programs, and G/M-code programs.
- Assist with operation and troubleshooting to maintain production requirements.
- Work alongside Maintenance to troubleshoot and repair CNC mills, lathes, and grinders on smaller mechanical or pneumatic components.
- Support troubleshooting and repair of pneumatic and hydraulic systems as needed.

Leadership, Communication & Continuous Improvement

- Assign workers to workstations as needed to meet production requirements.
- Monitor production and adjust work assignments, material supply, or machine operation when necessary.
- Train workers in equipment operation and reinforce safe, consistent work practices.
- Confer with supervisors to receive instructions and exchange production information.
- Communicate temporary and permanent process changes regularly to manufacturing and engineering.
- Assist with identifying and developing preventive maintenance activities tied to production processes and equipment.
- Support development, improvement, and problem-solving initiatives that improve machine uptime, quality, throughput, and process reliability.

Machine Care, Housekeeping & Maintenance Support

- Clean machine fixtures, load raw material, and prepare parts by deburring, sanding, or cleaning for fixture placement.
- Start up and shut down machines according to expectations.
- Monitor tool management systems and support proper tooling organization.
- Perform preventive maintenance activities on machines as assigned.
- Maintain clean equipment and work areas throughout the shift.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications & Abilities

- Strong CNC manufacturing background with thorough knowledge of cutting tools, CNC machine operation, and precision metal cutting processes.
- Ability to identify, analyze, and resolve CNC machining problems with urgency and sound judgment.
- Strong communication, leadership, and accountability skills.
- Ability to read and interpret engineering blueprints, process sheets, CMM reports, and basic CNC programs.
- Ability to read G/M-code programs and understand the principles of CNC machine operations.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to produce highly accurate parts.
- Basic math skills and the ability to complete production counts and related documentation accurately.
- Computer proficiency, including Windows-based software, Microsoft Excel, and Microsoft Word.
- Knowledge of geometric tolerance, shop mechanics, drafting, occupational hazards, and required safety precautions.
- Ability to recognize machine problems and take a proactive approach to machining issues.

Experience & Education

- High school diploma or GED required.
- Four to seven years’ minimum experience as a Machinist in a machine shop with horizontal and vertical machinery, Turning Centers, and Grinders.
- Technical school experience or equivalent CNC training preferred.
- Experience as a shift leader in a machining environment preferred.
- Strong background in shop mechanics, drafting, CNC machining, troubleshooting, and production support preferred.

Working Conditions & Physical Requirements

- This is a 24-hour manufacturing operation; availability to work weekends and overtime is required as business needs demand.
- Work is performed at a computer and on CNC machines in the Manufacturing area.
- Work requires standing for extended periods and frequent walking between machines and workstations.
- Personal protective equipment is required.
- Work may involve confined areas, uneven or slippery floors, oils, coolants, and cleaning solutions.
- Physical exertion may require lifting up to 50 pounds for short periods. Lifts in excess of safe individual limits may require assistance.
- Work requires delicate and controlled movements to locate small components in fixtures and vises.

Expectations for Success

This role requires a high level of ownership. The CNC Technician must be dependable, proactive, detail-oriented, and comfortable working independently while also supporting Operators, Supervisors, Maintenance, Quality, and Engineering. The position requires sound judgment under pressure, strong follow-through, and the ability to help protect production output without compromising Safety or Quality.

title: Quality Technician
description:
JOB SUMMARY / OBJECTIVE

Perform dimensional inspection of components and assemblies using optical comparators, precision hand gages, and coordinate measuring machines (CMMs). Support Manufacturing and Quality Engineering by documenting results, identifying nonconforming products, and helping resolve measurement and process issues.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

- Perform incoming, in-process, and final inspections to current engineering drawings, approved inspection plans, and work instructions.
- Set up and use optical comparators, micrometers, calipers, height gages, indicators, bore gages, and pin/plug gages; select methods appropriate to the feature and tolerance.
- Interpret dimensions, tolerances, datum references, and basic geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T); seek clarification when requirements are unclear.
- Operate CMMs using approved programs; verify part setup and equipment readiness, review reports, and recognize suspect results. Change released programs only with authorization.
- Record accurate, traceable inspection results. Identify and segregate nonconforming material, promptly escalate concerns, support containment, problem solving, and rework verification.

.OTHER JOB FUNCTIONS:

- Maintain accurate and detailed quality records as required by the department.
- Assist with the development and refinement of inspection procedures.
- Support continuous improvement initiatives across inspection processes and quality assurance.
- Perform other duties as assigned by the Quality Engineering team

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

Work is performed in inspection-lab and manufacturing settings and includes sitting, standing, close-tolerance visual inspection, and repetitive handling of components. Requires manual dexterity to position parts and use measuring equipment, and the ability to lift or transport containers weighing up to 40 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. Follow site safety requirements and applicable firearms-handling procedures after required training.

QUALIFICATIONS/ABILITIES:

- Demonstrated hands-on dimensional inspection experience using optical comparators, precision hand gages, and CMMs running established programs. Experience with any CMM software is acceptable.
- Ability to read engineering drawings and inspection instructions, interpret dimensional tolerances and basic GD&T, and apply shop mathematics and inch/metric conversions.
- Attention to detail, and disciplined documentation. Ability to question unusual results and distinguish potential measurement issues from product defects.
- Excel, and learning technical software; demonstrated problem-solving ability and a clear interest in CMM programming, metrology, and calibration responsibilities.
- Ability to work independently within approved procedures, communicate findings clearly, and coordinate priorities with Manufacturing and Quality Engineering.

EXPERIENCE\EDUCATION:

- Two or more years of hands-on manufacturing dimensional inspection experience, or equivalent practical experience demonstrating the required skills. Relevant machining experience with substantial inspection responsibility is acceptable.
- High school diploma or equivalent. Technical training, an apprenticeship, or an associate degree in machining, manufacturing, quality, or metrology is preferred.

title: Supplier Development Engineer
description:
The Supplier Development Engineer is a high-impact, hands-on role responsible for elevating supplier capability, accelerating performance recovery, and building a stronger, more reliable supply base for discrete manufacturing operations. This role partners aggressively with Supply Chain, Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, and suppliers to drive measurable gains in quality, delivery, cost, capacity, and launch readiness. The position requires a process-driven leader who can move quickly from diagnosis to action, apply lean tools at the source, remove barriers, and deliver sustained supplier performance improvement.

Key Responsibilities

- Build and execute aggressive supplier development plans for critical, high-risk, or underperforming suppliers supporting discrete manufacturing operations.
- Rapidly assess supplier manufacturing processes, quality systems, capacity, tooling, controls, staffing, and readiness to meet production requirements.
- Lead targeted improvement projects that increase quality, delivery, throughput, lead time performance, scrap reduction, and process stability.
- Drive supplier launch readiness for new product introductions, sourcing transitions, and supplier changes through APQP, PPAP, first article inspection, run-at-rate reviews, and production readiness assessments.
- Conduct on-site supplier audits, process capability reviews, risk assessments, and manufacturing feasibility evaluations with clear action plans and owners.
- Attack root causes using structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, 5 Whys, fishbone analysis, mistake-proofing, and verified corrective action.
- Partner with Supplier Quality to contain issues quickly, resolve nonconforming material concerns, eliminate recurring defects, and prevent supplier escapes.
- Collaborate with Purchasing and Strategic Sourcing to qualify stronger suppliers, evaluate capability, and support make-buy, resourcing, and localization decisions.
- Work with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering to resolve specification, drawing, tolerance, inspection, process control, and manufacturability issues that limit supplier performance.
- Use supplier performance data to expose trends, prioritize risk, trigger escalation, and focus resources on the highest-impact improvement opportunities.
- Deliver cost-reduction and value-improvement results through process optimization, yield improvement, waste elimination, manufacturability improvements, and lead time reduction.
- Build strong supplier relationships while creating clear accountability for commitments, corrective actions, timelines, and business results.
- Communicate supplier risks, action plans, technical findings, recovery status, and executive updates with clarity, urgency, and precision.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, or a related technical field.
- Three to seven years of experience in supplier development, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, quality engineering, process engineering, continuous improvement, or a related manufacturing role.
- Hands-on experience in a discrete manufacturing environment involving machined parts, fabricated components, castings, forgings, stampings, molded parts, assemblies, finishing processes, or other engineered components.
- Proven ability to operate in a process-driven manner using standards, documented workflows, visual controls, performance metrics, escalation routines, and disciplined follow-up.
- Demonstrated success applying lean tools such as value stream mapping, standard work, 5S, visual management, Kaizen, root cause analysis, error proofing, takt time, line balancing, waste reduction, and daily management systems.
- Strong bias for action with the ability to quickly diagnose supplier performance gaps, engage stakeholders, escalate barriers, and drive corrective actions to verified closure.
- High drive for results with a track record of improving supplier quality, delivery, lead time, productivity, cost, capacity, or launch performance through structured improvement projects.
- Experience with APQP, PPAP, FMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, capability studies, corrective action, and root cause analysis.
- Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, inspection plans, and technical requirements.
- Strong analytical, project management, communication, and supplier-facing problem-solving skills.
- Willingness and ability to travel to supplier sites to audit processes, resolve issues, validate corrective actions, and accelerate supplier development projects.

Preferred Qualifications

- Lean, Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, ISO 9001 Lead Auditor, or similar quality/manufacturing certification.
- Experience using lean daily management, tiered accountability, supplier scorecards, standard work audits, action registers, and visual performance boards to sustain improvement.
- Experience with ERP, supplier portals, quality management systems, statistical analysis tools, and manufacturing performance dashboards.
- Experience supporting regulated or highly controlled manufacturing environments such as automotive, aerospace, defense, firearms, industrial equipment, medical device, or precision machining.
- Experience leading cross-functional supplier recovery projects, rapid improvement events, capacity expansion plans, or supplier localization/resourcing initiatives with measurable results.

Core Competencies

- Process discipline: Operates through clear standards, repeatable methods, documented action plans, defined ownership, and consistent follow-up.
- Lean execution: Applies lean tools practically at supplier sites to remove waste, stabilize processes, improve flow, and sustain measurable performance gains.
- Bias for action: Moves quickly from issue identification to containment, root cause, corrective action, and verified closure without waiting for perfect information.
- Drive for results: Sets clear targets, measures progress, removes obstacles, and delivers improvements in quality, delivery, cost, capacity, and lead time.
- Structured problem solving: Uses data, observation, root cause analysis, and corrective action discipline to eliminate recurring supplier issues.
- Supplier influence and accountability: Builds productive supplier relationships while holding suppliers accountable to commitments, timelines, and performance expectations.
- Cross-functional collaboration: Works effectively with Supply Chain, Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Planning, and Operations leadership to accelerate execution.
- Data-driven decision making: Uses supplier scorecards, defect data, delivery performance, capacity analysis, and cost information to prioritize action.

Key Performance Indicators

- Improvement in supplier on-time delivery performance and recovery of delinquent or constrained suppliers.
- Reduction in supplier defects, nonconforming material trends, repeat issues, and quality escapes.
- Speed and effectiveness of corrective action closure, including verified recurrence prevention.
- Completion of supplier audits, risk assessments, launch readiness reviews, and PPAP/FAI approvals on time and with clear follow-through.
- Supplier capacity readiness to support production demand, surge requirements, and new product launches.
- Cost savings, productivity gains, scrap reduction, yield improvement, and lead time reduction delivered through supplier development projects.
- Timely execution of supplier recovery plans, escalation actions, executive updates, and measurable improvement milestones.

Reporting Relationship and Work Environment

This position typically reports to the Supply Chain organization and works closely with commodity managers, buyers, planners, quality engineers, manufacturing engineers, design engineers, and production leadership. The role operates in both office and manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with suppliers, including on-site visits to manufacturing facilities. Travel may be required based on supplier location, launch activity, performance risk, or urgent production needs.
